mr_title: Made HttpRequest.get_preferred_type() consider media type parameters.
mr_description:
HttpRequest.get_preferred_type() did not account for parameters in
Accept header media types (e.g., "text/vcard; version=3.0"). This caused
incorrect content negotiation when multiple types differed only by
parameters, reducing specificity as per RFC 7231 section 5.3.2
(https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7231.html#section-5.3.2).

This fix updates get_preferred_type() to treat media types with
parameters as distinct, allowing more precise and standards-compliant
matching.

Thanks to magicfelix for the report, and to David Sanders and Sarah
Boyce for the reviews.

expected_issues.title: Accepted media types sorted by specificity instead of quality
expected_issues.description:
accepted_types is now sorted by specificity before quality, so get_preferred_type() prefers a more specific but lower-quality media type over a higher-quality one.

Specificity should only decide which Accept entry applies to a given candidate type; the preference order between candidates must follow the q-values. With `Accept: text/html;q=0.8, application/json` (or `text/*;q=1, text/plain;q=0.1`), sorting by (specificity, quality) makes get_preferred_type() return the lower-quality type, breaking content negotiation per RFC 9110. Two orderings are needed: by quality for preference, by specificity for matching.
